Ai._comment_AnalysisRepair: Production policy for the analysis-output repair layer (Ai:AnalysisRepair, see AnalysisRepairOptions in Services/Ai/AiOptions.cs). This block MIRRORS base appsettings.json (Enabled:true, GuardOnly:true, Mode:GlossaryThenDynamic, glossary-on for all PerType) because prod currently serves Ollama-LOCAL models via Ai:FeatureModels (gemma4:12b / qwen3.5:9b / DictaLM-3.0) - a leaky tier where the deterministic glossary guard still earns its keep. KEEP IN SYNC with Ai:FeatureModels: the model actually served in prod. Do NOT make this a no-op on the assumption a cloud tier is leak-free: a 2026-07-10 3-passage cloud sweep (google/gemma-4-31b-it via OpenRouter) leaked English into Hebrew prose at the SAME ~1/3 rate as local gemma4:12b (local leaked 'confusion', cloud leaked 'claustrophobia'; both out-of-glossary abstract nouns). No measured tier is leak-free on this task, so keep the guard ON across tiers (it is a zero-cost no-op on clean fields). CAVEAT: the deterministic glossary only cleans its 23 curated craft terms (LiteraryTermGlossary.Terms), NOT the general-vocabulary leaks seen in the wild - a dynamic detect-and-repair replacement for the closed glossary (DynamicTermRepairService, dynamic-term-repair-design plan) EXISTS and is turned ON in prod via Mode=GlossaryThenDynamic (the span-scoped dynamic stage runs AFTER the glossary fast-path; flip Mode back to Glossary/Off to disable it, and Enabled=false remains the master off-switch). The ON default rests on the 2026-07-12 RE-MEASURE (be-c08, docs/ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_REPAIR.md section 18), which drove the REAL BookEntityProvider over a real DbContext on the shipped LOCAL gemma4:12b tier: out-of-glossary cleaning 100% (10/10), unchanged (delta 0 percentage points, 0 leaks spared) when an adversarial per-book entity set is active; legitimate-term preservation 100% (21/21) with 0 false positives; over-rewrite 0; and 0 legitimate values reaching the model, so precision here is a property of the DETERMINISTIC GATE rather than of the model tier. It SUPERSEDES the 2026-07-11 d5/d6 tables (section 17), which fed a hand-built entity set and therefore never exercised the harvest logic or the bookId threading that actually ship. KEEP THIS BLOCK IN SYNC with base appsettings.json: AnalysisRepairConfigParityTests.Mode_BaseAndProduction_AreEqual fails if the two Mode values diverge. Extension point (documented only, NOT implemented): a per-provider/per-model override on AnalysisRepairOptions is only needed if a single environment ever serves MULTIPLE tiers at once (e.g. some requests to a cloud model, others to local Ollama, in the same deployment) - see the AnalysisRepairOptions xmldoc in Services/Ai/AiOptions.cs for the full note. SummaryBatchWindowChapters (be-c03) also mirrors base appsettings.json - see its _comment_SummaryBatchWindowChapters for the full rationale; it bounds how many chapters the chapter-summary pass summarizes and repairs before committing, so an abort cannot discard a whole 80-chapter book's work. AnalysisRepairConfigParityTests.SummaryBatchWindowChapters_BaseAndProduction_AreEqual fails if the two values diverge.

AnalysisRepair._comment_PerTypeExclusions: h3 (analysis-repair-pertype-coverage-holes plan, 2026-07-28) makes two exclusions EXPLICIT rather than merely absent, so the decision is visible at the config surface instead of inferred from a missing line. An explicit false is semantically IDENTICAL to absence under AnalysisRepairGate.Evaluate (present-and-false and absent both return PerTypeExcluded) - NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE. Custom: DELIBERATELY false (d1) - its instruction is user-authored (req.CustomPrompt), so the output is legitimately English / bilingual / quoted / tabular, which falsifies the layer's foreign-script=leak premise; and repair cost is one model call per foreign WORD with no cap, so an English answer would be both mistranslated and a several-hundred-call GPU wedge. See the plan's '## d1 decision'. Synopsis: DELIBERATELY false (q1) - MEASURED on the shipped LOCAL tier (Ollama | gemma4:12b): preservation 83% (5/6) against the bar of >= 90% AND over-rewrite exactly 0 (over-rewrite was 0, cleaning passed 100%, but the bar is a conjunction); the repair model transliterated a legitimate sentence-initial proper noun (an author's name) at a paragraph head, reproduced identically on cloud gemma-4-31b-it, so it is structural (BookEntityProvider only harvests from the manuscript, never the external names/works/places a synopsis legitimately introduces) rather than a small-model artifact - and Synopsis is fed back into later analysis prompts as book-brief context, so a false positive there compounds. See the plan's '## q1 quality-gate results'. Proofread stays ABSENT rather than explicit-false: its exclusion is architectural (output quotes verbatim manuscript spans; repairing them would corrupt the suggestion diff), already stated independently in docs section 4 and inside all three dispatch switches' own default/fallback arms, and PerType is a map of things that MAY be flipped on - an explicit false here could misleadingly suggest Proofread is a config-level toggle, when enabling it would require rewriting the dispatch switches and would violate the verbatim-manuscript-span design rule. AnalysisRepairConfigParityTests.EveryAnalysisType_HasAnExplicitRepairCoverageDecision (h2) accepts absent OR present-and-false for all three, so this asymmetry between Custom/Synopsis and Proofread is a deliberate choice, not an inconsistency. KEEP THIS IN SYNC with the sibling appsettings file's own _comment_PerTypeExclusions (byte-identical) - AnalysisRepairConfigParityTests.PerType_BaseAndProduction_AreEqual only compares the boolean PerType values, not this comment, but drift here would make the two files' documented rationale disagree.
